extracted.intended_audience: NIMH/NIH grant applicants and principal investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the contents of NIMH summary statements produced after peer review and the policies that can create a 'bar to funding' which applicants must address before an application can be finalized for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall resume and summary of review discussion (if scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRA prepares the summary statement which contains: Overall resume and summary of review discussion (if scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement is posted within four weeks of the peer review committee meeting on eRA Commons and becomes the official Institute/Center record of the peer review committee recommendations. Contact the program officer listed on the summary statement for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques by the reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary statement contains critiques by the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reviewer critiques are included in the summary statement and should be read carefully to understand strengths and weaknesses identified by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority score and percentile ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority score and percentile ranking (if scored; also not all applications receive a percentile ranking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scored, the priority score and, where applicable, percentile ranking appear on the summary statement and indicate the review outcome relative to other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary statement contains budget recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget recommendations provided in the summary statement indicate reviewer or committee input on the appropriateness of the proposed budget and may guide programmatic funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary statement contains administrative notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative notes may include procedural comments, notices, or other non-scientific information relevant to the application's processing or eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bars to Funding — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, the following policies and regulations must be adequately addressed in the application. (See also Step 2.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these areas are not adequately addressed, a 'bar to funding' code may be listed on the summary statement beneath the score with a phrase stating the area is unacceptable. Such bars must be responded to by the applicant and 'lifted' before the application can be finalized and considered for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Human Subjects Policies and Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Human Subjects Policies and Guidance must be addressed when human subjects are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications involving human subjects must follow NIH human subjects policies; failure to adequately address these policies may trigger a bar to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women and Minorities As Participants In Research Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must adequately address the policy on inclusion of women and minorities as participants in research involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inclusion plan for women and minorities is inadequate, the summary statement may list a bar to funding which the applicant must respond to and correct before funding can proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children As Participants In Research Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must adequately address the policy on inclusion of children as participants in research involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to justify inclusion/exclusion of children or to follow applicable policies may result in a bar to funding that must be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vertebrate animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications involving vertebrate animals must adequately address relevant policies and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inadequate description or justification of vertebrate animal use can produce a bar to funding; the summary statement will list the code and the area deemed unacceptable and the applicant must respond to lift the bar.
